# Warrant v0 design inventory

This is the acceptance inventory for [VER04](../../VER04-warrant-language.md),
not an executed parser corpus. No Warrant parser/type checker or generated Rust
tests are supplied here. P006 will materialize syntax cases as data, generate
TFV and pin parse trees with independent negative controls. P007/P008 add the
later-phase checks below; they must not claim those checks from parse success.

An expected acceptance is always **phase specific**. A syntactically accepted
program can still fail typing, contracts, bindings or solver checks. Every
negative case must reach its named phase, fail with the named diagnostic and
point to the offending source span. Preceding unrelated failures do not satisfy
that case. Add a minimally changed accepted baseline for every rejection.

## Named acceptance cases

| Case | Phase | Required outcome / distinguishing change |
|---|---|---|
| V0-P001 | syntax/types | Bool true/false equality, Int/Nat widening and len are accepted |
| V0-P002 | syntax/types | Empty Bytes and widths zero/16 retain their declared types |
| V0-P003 | syntax/types | U64 sign-bit/max literals retain all 64 bits; modular addition wraps |
| V0-P004 | syntax/types | Exhaustive Option/Result matches produce their common arm type |
| V0-P005 | syntax/types | Forall/exists binders and left-to-right refinements scope correctly |
| V0-P006 | syntax/types | Both Bool selection choices and length-error Result compare correctly |
| V0-P007 | syntax/types | Bound/input/labels parse as contracts referring to actual op parameters |
| V0-P008 | source | CRLF source normalizes with original byte spans; TFV policy remains distinct |
| V0-N001 | source W0001 | BOM/NUL, leading tab, inconsistent dedent or each resource limit+1 rejects |
| V0-N002 | syntax W0101 | Odd/uppercase/invalid byte hex and unknown keyword/token reject |
| V0-N003 | syntax W0101 | Floating literal, host import/path/eval, scenario/set/budget unsupported profile rejects |
| V0-N004 | syntax W0102 | Missing result arrow, required expression or closing delimiter rejects |
| V0-N005 | names W0201 | Duplicate type/callable, example/claim name, contract or assume section rejects |
| V0-N006 | names W0202 | Unknown callable/type/error/label parameter is not guessed or imported |
| V0-N007 | names W0203 | Model recursion/alias cycle and binder shadowing reject |
| V0-N008 | types W0301 | Bool vs Int, wrong arity/result type or overflowing U64 literal rejects |
| V0-N009 | types W0301 | Bytes literal of wrong static width or dynamic Bytes passed as Bytes<16> rejects |
| V0-N010 | types W0301 | Nonexhaustive/duplicate match arm and context-free empty list/None reject |
| V0-N011 | contracts W0401 | Missing hostile input/steps/heap/depth, unknown ensures flag or negative bound rejects |
| V0-N012 | contracts W0402 | Environment assumption about hostile data through a model alias rejects |
| V0-N013 | contracts W0402 | Conflicting overlapping rejection errors or public label weakening inferred secret rejects |
| V0-N014 | bindings W0501 | Wrong/missing real export, argument constructor, observer or fixed width instantiation rejects |
| V0-N015 | bindings W0502 | Constant generator/observer and each surviving built-in subject mutant reject |
| V0-N016 | bindings W0502 | Aliasing either selection input fails fresh-output control; empty pointer equality alone does not |
| V0-N017 | solver W0601 | Inconsistent claims/assumptions, example contradiction, unreachable refinement or trivializing assumption rejects checked status |
| V0-N018 | evidence W0602 | Unknown/timeout/unchecked certificate/unavailable analyzer or resource observer never yields checked/proved |
| V0-N019 | evidence | Crypto/CT01 target with no discovered secret input fails vacuity; compare branch/address/step traces, not counts alone |
| V0-N020 | evidence | A sampled quantified claim, logical-work count or standalone export list cannot be promoted to universal proof, measured steps or complete API coverage |
| V0-N021 | generation | Missing target emits blocked/not-live with nonzero complete-pilot acceptance, never an ok/true placeholder |
| V0-N022 | generation | Reordered registration retains TF01 identities/sub-seeds; stale generated bytes fail regeneration |

V0-N018 includes unavailable observation/checking infrastructure. Its diagnostic
is W0602 rather than pretending the source formula itself is false. V0-N019
uses W0601 for the no-secret-input vacuity condition and W0602 when the required
analyzer/proof layer is unavailable; the fixture must identify which condition
it deliberately establishes. V0-N020–022 pin evidence/generation records as well
as source; they cannot be certified by a parser-only test.

## Complete source examples for early phases

The following program is a positive source/name/type example. It declares no
subject operations and claims no shipped-code evidence. A future model checker
must still check it before reporting checked-spec status.

```text
warrant values
  assume platform:
    none
  assume environment:
    none
  example bool_values:
    true != false
  example bytes_length:
    len(b"00ff") == 2
  example word_wrap:
    18446744073709551615u64 + 1u64 == 0u64
  example safe_division:
    div(7, 0) == None
  example safe_index:
    at(b"00", 1) == None
```

`None` has a contextual Option<Int>/Option<U8> type in the final two examples.
These exercise total operations; the language has no implicit unwrap that can
turn a missing value into successful data.

V0-N008's minimal type-negative source changes only the example expression:

```text
warrant bad_bool
  assume platform:
    none
  assume environment:
    none
  example mismatch:
    true == 1
```

Expect W0301 at the incompatible comparison; changing `1` to `false` restores
the accepted baseline. A host language treating true as 1 must not influence
Warrant's own type rules.

V0-N017's reachability-negative source is parse/name/type valid:

```text
warrant unreachable
  assume platform:
    none
  assume environment:
    none
  claim empty_domain:
    forall n: Nat | n < 0. n == n
```

Nat is nonnegative, so the admitted domain is empty. The formula is true in
ordinary logic; that does not make it a useful verification claim. A solver
that demonstrates unreachability causes W0601; absent that solver, checked
status is incomplete (W0602), never silently successful.

## Promotion and review

Before P006 promotes this inventory to an executed corpus, it must document
the grammar version, all source limits and exact source-span mapping. Cases
stay data: no embedded Rust, shell, Python step definitions or expected answers
derived by invoking the same parser/checker being tested. Runtime readers use
TFV; JSON may remain its authoring format. Tests must show each negative
validator fires, and the runner's sabotage must fail.

Public enablement of new claim/property/fuzz or generator runs remains subject
to VER26 §10's private-first requirement. This directory publishes language
design examples, not a randomized campaign or a release decision.
